**Voica v0.8.0 — the "э-э-э" goes, the quotes come out paired, and every rule that changes your words now has a switch.**

### New: filler sounds are removed

The drawn-out "э-э-э", "ммм", "хмм" mean nothing in speech and clutter the text. Voica now takes
them out by rule — no key, no network, both engines — and it is on by default.

The rule reads the **shape** of a word rather than a list of spellings: a token that collapses to
one or two letters once hyphens and repeated letters are folded. Listing spellings would be
hopeless, because recognition writes the same mumble differently every single time.

What it deliberately leaves alone matters more than what it removes, and every one of these is a
line of real text that broke while the rule was being built:

- single sounds go **only when they were drawn out** — on its own "а" is a conjunction, "у" and "о"
  are prepositions;
- **"и" is never touched at all**: the engine writes the abbreviation "ИИ" in lower case too, and
  "Проверка ии" was becoming "Проверка";
- **"эм" is not a filler** — that is how the engine spells GigaAM;
- **numbers and all-caps abbreviations are untouchable**, and "мм" after a number is millimetres;
- a real word that was merely drawn out is **straightened, not dropped**: "Ну-у-у" → "Ну". The list
  of those is explicit, or "PPC" would become "Pc".

Turn it off if you transcribe speech verbatim — unlike the term rules, this one deletes what was
said, so it is the one rule where a setting is genuinely owed to you.

### New: quotation marks are repaired

Straight quotes become proper guillemets, decided by position; a space missing after a colon comes
back; unpaired marks are removed. It runs last, right before the text is delivered — after both the
term rules and the AI pass, because either can leave a mess and there is no telling which did. The
engine decodes greedily and has no memory of having opened a quote; the model likes to wrap a
substituted term in quotes against the explicit ban in its prompt.

English text is left alone: guillemets are Russian typography, and in an English dictation straight
quotes are correct.

### New: a switch for every rule that changes your words

Filler removal and quote repair sit under **Text clean-up** on the Dictation tab; **Fix terms by
rules** sits on Vocabulary above the AI pass — first what always works and costs nothing, then the
optional extra. All three are on by default. The reason for having them at all is simple: without a
switch, a rule that ever gets one of *your* words wrong could only be escaped by waiting for an
update.

### New: the first run without a key is not a dead end

With no key saved, Settings opens on the key field and reads as "no key, no dictation" — while the
local engine needs neither key nor internet. A line under the field now says so, and only when it
applies: cloud engine selected, no key saved.

### Fixed

- **A phrase could be duplicated where two windows meet**, when they split the same place into a
  different number of words — "3кар" against "Три кар" is four words against five, and matching them
  word by word has nothing to line up. A fallback now compares the words glued together without
  spaces.
- **A filler opening a sentence mid-text left the next word in lower case** — "…на улицу. Э-э, на
  работу" came out as "…на улицу. на работу". Found by running the rules over a whole real history,
  three times in a single dictation.

### Install

Windows 10 1809+ / x64:

| File | Size | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **`Voica-Setup-0.8.0.exe`** | ~75 MB | nothing — recommended |
| `Voica.exe` | ~80 MB | nothing — single file, no installation |
| `Voica-fx.exe` | ~37 MB | [.NET 8 Desktop Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0) installed once |

Installing over an existing copy keeps your history, settings and API key.

Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn → **More info → Run anyway**
([why, and how to verify](https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win#why-does-windows-warn-about-this-app)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/Inhum/voica-win/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
